newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - July 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - July 4.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- Central committees of China's eight non-Communist parties and the All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce meet to discuss President Jiang Zemin's Hong Kong handover speeches.
- The 26th Session of the Standing Committee of the Eighth National People's Congress concludes
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH
- Premier Li Peng meet in Beijing with Juergen Sarrazin, chairman of the board of directors of the Dresdner Bank Group of Germany.
- Sultan Tuanku Ja'afar, supreme head of state of Malaysia, will pay a state visit to China from July 8 to 15.
- A delegation of the House of Representatives of the National Assembly of Thailand, led by First Deputy Speaker Sophon Phetsawang will visit China from July 4 to 8.
CHINA DAILY
- A Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman warns the Philippine navy's recent activities on the Nansha Islands are "another serious infringement on China's sovereignty."
CHINA SECURITIES
- China to join an international accounting organisation next week
ECONOMIC INFORMATION DAILY
- China is to encourage poverty-stricken farmers to rear ostriches.
- A survey has found the Jetta sedan is the best known car brand name in China.
INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS DAILY
- Henan province is expected to produce 15,000 tonnes of andalusite in 1997, mostly for export.
ECONOMIC DAILY
- A State Statistical Bureau survey shows income of employees in transport and telecommunications rose 390 pct in 1991-6
FINANCIAL NEWS
- China is to license its silk reeling and spinning industry.
